_comment: Hand-written expectations for SQL lineage extraction (DuckDB dialect). Used by tests/test_sql_lineage.py and demo/scripts/lineage_parser_scorecard.py. 'reads' and 'writes' are asset names, order-insensitive.

cases.why: the simplest thing that must work
cases.sql: SELECT id, amount FROM orders

cases.why: a CTE name is scope, not an asset
cases.sql: WITH recent AS (SELECT * FROM orders) SELECT id FROM recent
WITH a AS (SELECT * FROM orders), b AS (SELECT * FROM a JOIN customers c ON c.id = a.cid) SELECT * FROM b

cases.why: a qualified name is never a CTE reference
cases.sql: WITH orders AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT * FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT id FROM public.orders

cases.why: text matching invents a table here
cases.sql: SELECT 'shipped from warehouse' AS note FROM orders

-- reload FROM nowhere
SELECT * FROM orders
/* JOIN legacy_orders here one day */ SELECT * FROM orders
SELECT * FROM 'data/raw_data.json'
SELECT * FROM read_csv('data/orders.csv')

cases.why: a file and a table in one query
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM read_parquet('data/x.parquet') p JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.id
MERGE INTO dim_customer d USING stg_customer s ON d.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = s.name
UPDATE orders SET status = 'x' WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM cancellations)
DELETE FROM orders WHERE id < 5

cases.why: a view is an asset the pipeline produces
cases.sql: CREATE VIEW daily AS SELECT day, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY day

cases.why: CTAS, with a schema on the source
cases.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t AS SELECT * FROM public.orders
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t AS SELECT * FROM orders
INSERT INTO fact_orders SELECT * FROM stg_orders

cases.why: a table can be both read and written
cases.sql: INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM t WHERE x > 1

cases.why: public.orders and orders are one asset
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM public.orders o JOIN orders x ON x.id = o.id

cases.why: quoting is meaningful in a case-sensitive catalog
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM "Weird Name"
SELECT * FROM ORDERS

cases.why: a derived table is scope, its source is the asset
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 0) x
SELECT a.id FROM orders a JOIN orders b ON b.parent_id = a.id
SELECT id FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT id FROM archived_orders
SELECT id FROM orders EXCEPT SELECT id FROM cancellations

cases.why: window syntax must not confuse source detection
cases.sql: SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cid ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders

cases.why: one config field can hold several statements
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE stg AS SELECT * FROM raw_orders; INSERT INTO fact SELECT * FROM stg;
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1), (2)
